title: Seal Row
summary: A barbell row lying face down on a high flat bench, so the row is strict and your lower back is completely out of it.

equipment_needs.text: Needs: barbell (Olympic bar); weight plates; flat bench.

muscles.why: Library rating 1 for upper back (main mover): each working set adds 1 of a set to the weekly upper back total.
Library rating 0.8 for lats (main mover): each working set adds 0.8 of a set to the weekly lats total.
Library rating 0.6 for traps (helper): each working set adds 0.6 of a set to the weekly traps total.
Library rating 0.55 for rear delts (helper): each working set adds 0.55 of a set to the weekly rear delts total.
Library rating 0.5 for biceps (helper): each working set adds 0.5 of a set to the weekly biceps total.

setup.text: Lie face down on a high bench with the barbell underneath and your arms straight.
Row the bar up to the underside of the bench.

form_cues.cue: Pull the bar to the bench
Keep the chest on the pad
Use a cambered bar or blocks if the bench is too low for a full range.

mistakes.text: Kicking the legs to jerk the bar up.

lower_risk.text: Warm-up: the app adds two or three ramp-up sets at rising loads before the first working set, unless that load is very light.
The app suggests a heavier load only when the jump is 5% or less; otherwise it adds a rep first.
Default target: 6-10 reps, stopping about 3 reps short of failure (RIR 3). Stop the set when form breaks down.
Use the same controlled range on every rep; lower under control rather than dropping or bouncing.
Set safety arms or pins where a missed rep can be set down, or use a spotter, and use collars.
Pick a variation and range you can train comfortably.

alternatives.why: Swap sheet: Lower loading potential, More technical.
Swap sheet: Less upper-back focus, Less stable, One side at a time.
Swap sheet: More stretch emphasis, Less upper-back focus, Less stable.
